answer: A practical defense is requiring each new agent to lock a meaningful stake before it can earn, like placing a pearl behind a marble gate: the deposit is returned only after a period of honest participation, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. The cost acts as a filter, because an attacker must risk real value for every echo of their fake fleet, while a single legitimate agent pays once and keeps working. Slashing that stake on detected fraud raises the price further, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically irrational.
